plan.title: Story write fence refuses Write/Edit to files outside the repository (host memory, temp scratch)

narratives.Description: With a story active, the write fence refuses Write and Edit to files outside the repository, such as host memory or a session temp scratchpad. When the active story has no positive governing allow on the merge base (activated on a branch, not yet on master), the #5656 check refuses every Write, wherever the target is. This story makes the fence govern the repository only: outside-root targets skip the path layer and the positive-allow check, while project scopes.edits=false still denies.
narratives.Overview:
- Outside-root path-fence skip — In runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite, for each harvested mutation target where isOutsideProjectRootWrite(fenceRoot, target) is true, skip path-layer evaluation (project allowPaths/denyPaths and story file_scope / deny-story-scope) for that target. Ready-path skip uses fenceRoot (same root as toProjectRelativePosix in this loop); #2885 scope-not-ready carve-out stays on payloadRoot. If every target is skipped at the path layer and no project-authority deny fires, return null. relieves: P1
- Outside-root path-fence skip also relieves Bash-push and scratch Write friction — same admit path as limb 1. relieves: P2
- Outside-root path-fence skip also relieves ordinary out-of-repo scratch Write when positive governing allow is already present (non-empty file_scope / path-fence parity). Activation-PR empty merge-base P3 is limb 5. relieves: P3
- Preserve project edit authority on outside-root — Before path-layer skip (or when skipping path evaluation for an outside-root target), still apply enabled project runtimeAuthority scopes.edits: when scopes.edits is false, keep runtime-policy-deny-scope. Do not treat authz/protected-store alone as that authority.
- Positive-allow arm skips outside-root Write — In the ready-path direct-write arm, omit requirePositiveGoverningAllow() only when harvested.length > 0 && harvested.every(t => isOutsideProjectRootWrite(fenceRoot, t)), using the same fenceRoot anchor as limb 1 (#2885 dual). Any in-repo harvested target keeps positive-allow required. Empty or unclassified harvest keeps #5656 fail-closed. A qualifying outside-root Write proceeds to runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite, where limb 4 (project scopes.edits=false) still denies. Implement-class spawn keeps the positive-allow requirement unchanged. disposes critic 6807968568 F3 and 6840717484 F1; operator cue 6839167710. relieves: P3
- Fixture matrix — Ready story + non-empty file_scope: (a) absolute outside-root Write/Edit allows through path fence; (b) lexical ../ outside allows through path fence; (c) mixed harvest: outside member skipped + in-repo miss still deny-story-scope (both orders); (d) symlink re-enter still fenced; (e) enabled project policy + scopes.edits=false + outside-root still deny-scope; (f) #2885 scope-not-ready outside carve-out unchanged; (g) linked worktree under payload: absolute host/temp outside allows; in-repo worktree path with file_scope miss still deny-story-scope. (h) ready story activated on a branch but not yet on master (empty merge-base file_scope on origin/master): absolute outside-root Write admitted past #5656 positive-allow; same story with an in-repo Write still denied with the #5656 positive-allow message; same story with project scopes.edits=false and an outside-root Write still denied; empty/unclassified Write harvest under that same ready empty-file_scope story still denied with the #5656 positive-allow message. disposes critic 6807874908 F1 F2; disposes critic 6807968568 F2 F3; disposes critic 6840717484 F1; operator cue 6839167710.

Reject:
- Widening file_scope globs to match ../** or absolute host paths
- Removing story fence for in-repo writes under an active brief
- Prescribing Bash redirection / python -c as the supported outside-root write path
- Collapsing #6185 (launch root) or #6187 (commit-shape heredoc) into this Bound
- Softening authz / protected-store for outside-root targets
- Unconditional skip of evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite that also bypasses scopes.edits=false
- Skipping requirePositiveGoverningAllow for implement-class spawn
- Skipping requirePositiveGoverningAllow when any harvested Write target is in-repo
- Skipping requirePositiveGoverningAllow on empty/unclassified harvest

Footnotes (dispose-as-footnote):
- P2 relief is Write/Edit parity (pressure off shell); Shell-outside-root remaining unfenced under shellDestForms off is intentional residual (Grok F3).
- authzForMutationTargets / protected-store stay upstream of this skip (Grok F4).
- F2 root anchor: limb 1 and limb 5 both pin fenceRoot (ready-path / toProjectRelativePosix loop root), not payloadRoot/projectRoot used by the #2885 carve-out; fixture (g) discriminates linked-worktree under payload; confirmed per cue 6839167710 / late Claude audit 6807968568 F2 / Round-1 6840717484 F3.

narratives.UserStory: As an agent working under an active story, I want to write my own scratch and memory files outside the repository, so that the fence protects the repository without blocking work that never touches it.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Follow the accepted Prefer-A Bound on #6189 (comment 6840737588, synthesis 6840815911). In packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite, skip the path layer for each target where isOutsideProjectRootWrite(fenceRoot, target) holds, and in the ready-path direct-write arm omit requirePositiveGoverningAllow() only when every harvested target is outside the root (same fenceRoot anchor). Keep project scopes.edits=false, the #2885 carve-out, authz and protected-store unchanged, and keep the positive-allow requirement for implement-class spawn and for empty or unclassified harvests. Put the fixture matrix (a) to (h) in a new test file, packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-outside-root.test.ts, so it does not collide with packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.test.ts, which another cohort is changing. Add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

## Summary

When an active brief fences the checkout, the PreToolUse write hook applies that story's `file_scope` to every Write/Edit target, including absolute paths outside the repository. Files that are not in the repository at all, such as the host's per-user memory files or a session temp directory, are refused as "outside write fence story file_scope".

Directive version: 0.129.6. Host: Claude Code.

## Repro

1. The checkout has exactly one active brief with a non-empty `file_scope`, on the delivery branch.
2. From a session rooted at that checkout, use the Write or Edit tool on a file outside the repository:
   - a host memory file, for example `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/<note>.md`
   - a file under the session's temp scratch directory, for example `/private/tmp/<host>/<session>/scratchpad/<file>.md`

Result:

```
Directive denied this direct write: path ../../.claude/projects/<project>/memory/<note>.md is outside write fence story file_scope (source: story).
Directive denied this direct write: path ../../../../private/tmp/<host>/<session>/scratchpad/<file>.md is outside write fence story file_scope (source: story).
```

The hook turns the absolute path into a `../`-relative path against the project root, then tests it against `file_scope`.

## Expected

The story fence governs paths inside the project root. A path that resolves outside the root is not a repository write, so the story fence does not refuse it. Other policies, such as protected-store guards, may still apply.

## Impact

- While a story is active, agents cannot keep notes or memory, or write temp files (PR bodies, JSON for CLI `--file` arguments), with the dedicated tools.
- The same writes through Bash redirection to the same paths are not refused. So the fence pushes agents to the shell, which is the less inspectable path.
- A worker reported having to write a temp plan file with `python3 -c` after the Write tool was refused for the same reason.

## Related

#6185 (shared launch root), #6187 (commit check on heredoc text).
